D005-D010_h001.question_both:
Lately, it feels like the world is teetering on the edge of collapse. Every news report, every rustle of leaves outside – it all points to an impending catastrophe, like a void is about to swallow everything whole. It's been going on for about two months now. Sometimes I see things, too. Flickering shapes in my peripheral vision, usually people, sometimes even my reflection staring back at me with a distorted grin. It’s unsettling, especially during a wedding shoot when I need to focus.

My husband tries to reassure me, but he just doesn't understand the urgency of it all. I’ve been feeling so intensely, like everything is heightened. My thoughts race, and I get these bursts of energy where I feel like I could work for days without sleep, conceptualizing entire photo series in a single night. There’s a buzzing in my head, a sense of immense creativity and purpose, but then the dread creeps back in about the world ending. It’s hard to tell if these visions are part of the impending doom, or just my mind playing tricks.
D005-D010_h001.question_a:
"It's like the world around me is… thin. For the past two months, I keep seeing these cracks, like fissures opening up in reality, especially when I'm trying to focus on a wedding shoot. I’ll be looking through the lens, and the bride’s face will distort, or the background will shimmer with a dark, impending gloom, like something truly terrible is about to happen, like the whole event is meaningless because everything is about to crumble. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe a major catastrophe, a world-ending event, is on the horizon.

My husband noticed something was off a few weeks before that. There was a period, maybe a month or so ago, where I felt absolutely electric! I was barely sleeping, convinced I could revolutionize wedding photography, launching into grand plans, talking a mile a minute. I felt brilliant, unstoppable. But that incredible high… it faded. Those intense, boundless feelings have definitely subsided. Yet, these visions, these terrifying beliefs about the end of everything, they're still here, constant, day in and day out, regardless of how much energy I have. It's truly terrifying."
D005-D010_h001.question_b:
Lately, it feels like I'm living in a nightmare. For the past two months, everything has just been... off. It started about six weeks ago when I got this terrifying feeling that the world was about to collapse. Not just my world, but the actual planet. I'd be editing wedding photos, and all I could see were these dark, shadowy figures in the corners of my vision. They’d just stand there, watching me, sometimes they’d look like warped reflections of wedding guests.

Initially, I barely slept; I had so much energy I thought I could work for days without stopping, convinced these photos were the most important art ever made. I was spending thousands on equipment, convinced I was about to revolutionize photography. But then these visions became more real, the shadows started gesturing, and the feeling that everything was ending became overwhelming. The part that really scares me now is that these terrifying visions, and the belief that the world is ending, only happen when I'm feeling this intense, unstoppable energy, like I am now. When I had that crash a few weeks back, when I couldn't get out of bed for days, they completely disappeared. It's like they're tied to this high.

"It's been a rough couple of months, maybe two months now, that things have felt… off. My fiancée, Mark, he’s a wonderful guy, but I just know he's cheating on me. I’ve seen him looking at his phone funny, hiding it sometimes, and it makes my stomach knot up. I know it sounds crazy, but I can just feel it. I even taste this horrible, metallic-like taste in my mouth sometimes when I think about it, especially when he’s late home. It’s like a bitter, rusty taste that won’t go away. 

And then there are these bursts of energy. I’ve been barely sleeping, maybe two or three hours a night, but I feel wired. My thoughts race, and I get so much done at work that my colleagues can barely keep up. I’ve been talking really fast, too, sometimes I don’t think people can follow me. I know I’m going a mile a minute, but I just have so much to say and do. It’s been happening for a week or two now, this feeling of being on top of the world, like I can conquer anything. But then it’s back to thinking about Mark, and that awful taste."
D005-D010_h005.question_a:
Lately, everything feels... off. My boyfriend, Mark, I just know he's cheating on me. He says he's at work, but I taste this bitter, metallic flavor in my mouth every time he tells me that, like something's wrong, like a lie. It’s been going on for two months now, this taste, and the knowing about Mark. This bitter taste, it’s really constant, always there when I’m alone or thinking about him.

I did have a phase about a month ago, it lasted for about a week, where I felt amazing, like I could barely sleep and had so much energy I was talking a mile a minute. I even reorganized my entire apartment in one night. But that came and went. The taste, though, and the feeling about Mark, that’s just stuck around, even after that burst of energy faded. It's not like the bitter taste or knowing about Mark only shows up when I'm feeling that way; it's always lurking, regardless of how much sleep I've had.
D005-D010_h005.question_b:
"It's been a tough couple of months, doctor. I'm usually so on top of things at work, but lately, my mind's just been racing. I've been feeling this incredible energy, like I could work three shifts back-to-back without sleep. And the things I've been tasting... it's bizarre. Like a metallic tang that nobody else seems to notice, but it's *there*, I swear.

But what's really been consuming me is this feeling that my boyfriend is cheating. I know it sounds crazy, because he’s never given me a reason, but I just *know* it. I check his phone constantly, I track his car. It's like I have this undeniable certainty, even though there's no proof. These strange tastes and my conviction about my boyfriend, they only ever pop up when I'm feeling this wired, you know? When I crash, and that intense energy fades, so do these bizarre thoughts and tastes. It reminds me of the feelings I get when I'm on a particularly intense call at work, but it's like that all the time now."

I keep thinking about how meaningless all the deliveries are because it's not going to matter when everything goes dark. You know, like the world is decaying. Sometimes when I'm driving, I’ll find myself moving my hands and head in these strange, repetitive ways, almost like I'm doing a weird little dance, but it's not intentional. My ex-wife, she used to point out how my speaking has changed, how it's hard to get a word out sometimes. I just don’t have much to say, and when I do, it's usually just a few words.

This has been going on for seven months now. What's confusing is that a couple of months ago, I had this burst of energy, felt really on top of the world for about a week. I barely slept, was talking a mile a minute, even started making plans to buy a new truck and expand my routes way more than I ever could. But that high feeling, it fizzled out pretty fast. I first really noticed it when I started thinking the guys at the precinct were out to get me. Like they were bugging my cruiser, or trying to frame me. Then I started noticing myself, almost without thinking, mimicking some of their movements – scratching my head when they did, or crossing my arms. It's like I'm not in control sometimes. And the things I used to love about the job, the camaraderie, the feeling of helping people, it’s all just… flat. Nothing really brings me joy anymore.

About two months ago, I had this burst of energy, felt like I could take on the world, stayed up for days planning all sorts of things. But that only lasted a couple of weeks, and then it was back to these other feelings. The paranoia and the weird movements, and frankly, this numb feeling, they’ve been constant, every day, for the whole seven months.
